A1:
**A1 — Calls isAvailable with a String argument (1 point)**

Award the point if anywhere in the response there is at least one syntactically correct invocation of the availability method made on the class `Account`, on `this`, on a reference whose type is `Account`, or with no receiver at all, and passed an argument evidently intended as the candidate username string. Grade generously on each of these aspects at once:

*Receiver.* A call on an `Account` object reference — e.g., `acct.isAvailable(s)` or `new Account(...).isAvailable(s)` — still counts as a call "on Account," since the receiver is an `Account` and the call compiles; the restriction exists only to exclude calls made on unrelated classes or objects (e.g., on a `String`, a `Scanner`, or a student-invented class). An unqualified call such as `isAvailable(requestedName)` inside the `Account` class counts as an implicit call on the class/`this`, which "use of `this` is optional" permits. Deduct on this aspect only when the sole invocation uses an explicit receiver that is something other than `Account` or `this`.

*Argument.* The argument need not be `requestedName`; the rubric explicitly tolerates passing a String other than the parameter. Do not deduct so long as the argument is evidently meant to be the candidate username string — an undeclared name variable, a value the student treats as text, or a call written with the type word included all count. Deduct only when the argument is clearly not intended as a string, such as a bare loop counter used as a number.

*Method name.* Do not deduct for minor spelling or capitalization variants (`isAvailible`, `IsAvailable`, `is_available`) when context makes the intended call to the availability method unambiguous; the point is for making the call.

*Multiple calls.* If one invocation meets the above standard, award the point even if another stray or leftover invocation elsewhere in the response is malformed.

Deduct only when there is no correct call anywhere — that is, when every invocation either is made on something other than `Account`/`this`/an `Account` reference, or passes an argument clearly not intended as a string, or is otherwise malformed.
A2:
**A2 — Updates potential usernames until an available username is found.**

Award the point when the loop both (a) calls the availability check and (b) re-tests a candidate that actually changes from iteration to iteration. Concretely, the availability check in the loop condition (or at the top of the loop body) must be passed the mutable candidate variable that holds the numbered name — e.g. `while (!Account.isAvailable(newUsername))` where `newUsername` is reassigned inside the loop to `requestedName + count` — so that each newly formed name is the thing being tested. This counts as no_deduct even if the availability call itself is made incorrectly in other respects (wrong receiver, wrong argument form), even if `requestedName` is not used, and even if the way the potential username is updated is otherwise wrong, so long as some candidate variable is updated in the body and that same variable is what the check sees.

Deduct when the response never calls the availability-checking method at all, when the check is made without any potential username being passed to it, when nothing in the body of the loop updates a potential username, or when the availability check is re-evaluated against the fixed original parameter (e.g. repeatedly calling `isAvailable(requestedName)` while only a counter or a separate unused variable changes), since in that case no new name is ever actually tested and the loop cannot terminate on an available username.
